<div class="nv-rule" id="shape-rules">

## Every `Core` member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#shape-rules"><code>core-api/shape-rules</code></a>
</div>

Every member of every `Core` class obeys all twenty shape rules below. A proposed member that cannot is a
design bug rather than an exception, and the rules are decided before the library is written because a
surface of ~450 members is only learnable if the eleventh member is predictable from the first ten.

| # | The rule |
|---|---|
| R1 | The subject is parameter 1, always ([`core-api/subject-first`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#subject-first "The subject is parameter 1 of every Core member, with no exceptions")) |
| R2 | Then required arguments in dataflow order, then at most one trailing optional shape literal ([`core-api/options-bag`](/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/#options-bag "A member's optional knobs are one trailing shape literal, never a flag or a bitmask")), every parameter callable by name ([`core-api/parameters-are-callable-by-name`](/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/#parameters-are-callable-by-name "Every Core parameter is callable by the name the spec writes, and that name is compatibility surface")) |
| R3 | Nothing mutates and nothing takes a reference ([`core-api/nothing-mutates`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#nothing-mutates "No Core member mutates its argument and none takes a reference")) |
| R4 | Failure throws; absence is `?T` ([`core-api/failure-throws`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#failure-throws "A Core member throws on failure and returns ?T for absence; false is never an answer")) |
| R5 | A fixed verb lexicon, and a closed ban list ([`core-api/verb-lexicon`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#verb-lexicon "A member's verb predicts its return type, and …OrNull, …Safe, …Ex and every try… but tryParse are banned")) |
| R6 | Symmetric operations get symmetric names ([`core-api/symmetric-names`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#symmetric-names "A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste")) |
| R7 | Members are full words ([`core-api/members-are-full-words`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#members-are-full-words "A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list")) |
| R8 | One range convention, `(offset, ?length)` ([`core-api/one-range-convention`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-range-convention "Every range is (offset, ?length), and a negative counts from the end")) |
| R9 | Callbacks receive `($value, $key)` ([`core-api/callback-receives-value-and-key`](/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/#callback-receives-value-and-key "A callback always receives ($value, $key), and may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes")) |
| R10 | Haystack before needle, subject before pattern — R1's corollary |
| R11 | No mode strings; an enum instead ([`core-api/no-mode-strings`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-mode-strings "A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt")) |
| R12 | Units are types ([`core-api/units-are-types`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#units-are-types "A unit is a type: a duration is a Duration and a size is uint bytes")) |
| R13 | A `string` member never takes an encoding argument ([`core-api/no-encoding-argument`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-encoding-argument "A string member never takes an encoding argument")) |
| R14 | Anything with a lifetime is an object ([`core-api/a-lifetime-is-an-object`](/docs/rules/core-api/lifetimes-and-absences/#a-lifetime-is-an-object "Anything with a lifetime is an object, and Core never hands back a handle")) |
| R15 | One name, one signature ([`core-api/one-name-one-signature`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#one-name-one-signature "One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names")) |
| R16 | A domain class is a singular noun ([`core-api/a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun`](/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun "A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it")) |
| R17 | One paradigm per operation; nothing is reachable two ways ([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-paradigm-per-operation "No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods")) |
| R18 | A domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods ([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-paradigm-per-operation "No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods")) |
| R19 | Scalars and `array<T>` never gain methods ([`core-api/no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays "A scalar and an array<T> never gain methods")) |
| R20 | No mutable/immutable twin types ([`core-api/no-mutable-immutable-twins`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-mutable-immutable-twins "Every Core value type is immutable, so no mutable twin exists to choose between")) |

Three properties of the language are what make PHP's conventions unavailable rather than merely ugly:
arrays are copy-on-write values, so a by-reference mutator has no performance argument left; types are
declared and checked, so a `false` return and an `int` flag mask throw away what the compiler already
knows; and there is no ambient state for a member to read ([`core-api/no-ambient-state`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-ambient-state "No Core member reads ambient state: there is no default timezone, locale, array pointer or error global")).

What this costs is familiarity. A PHP developer knows `sort($a)`, `strtotime` and `ob_start`, and none of
them survives in that spelling — each is named with its replacement so a diagnostic can point at one.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP's built-ins have no API at all — argument order, failure signalling and option encoding vary between neighbouring functions in the same extension</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="subject-first">

## The subject is parameter 1 of every `Core` member, with no exceptions

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#subject-first"><code>core-api/subject-first</code></a>
</div>

The thing a member operates on is its first parameter, including where the member also takes a callback or
a needle: `Arr::map($array, $fn)`, `Str::replace($subject, $search, $replacement)`,
`Arr::contains($haystack, $needle)`. Haystack comes before needle and subject before pattern, which is the
same rule stated for the two places PHP violates it most visibly.

A rule with no exceptions is learnable in one sentence, and the alternative is what PHP has: `array_map`
takes the callback first and `array_filter` takes the array first, so every call site is a lookup. The cost
is that a converted program's argument order changes at nearly every built-in call, which `nvs convert`
rewrites by pattern rather than by table.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>array_map(f, a)</code> beside <code>array_filter(a, f)</code>, and <code>in_array</code>, <code>str_replace</code> and <code>preg_match</code> disagreeing about haystack-before-needle, all become one order</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#shape-rules" title="Every Core member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20"><code>core-api/shape-rules</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#one-name-one-signature" title="One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names"><code>core-api/one-name-one-signature</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/arr-map-and-filter.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/arr-map-and-filter.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="verb-lexicon">

## A member's verb predicts its return type, and `…OrNull`, `…Safe`, `…Ex` and every `try…` but `tryParse` are banned

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#verb-lexicon"><code>core-api/verb-lexicon</code></a>
</div>

One verb means one thing, so a member's name predicts its return type. `is…`, `has…`, `contains` and
`startsWith` answer `bool`; `find…` answers `?T`; `indexOf` and `keyOf` answer `?uint` or `?K`; `count…`
answers `uint`; `to…` and `from…` convert and construct. Two constructor spellings join them: the unit or
component a value is built from (`Duration::seconds`, `TimeOfDay::at`), and `of` for a canonical identifier
(`Zone::of`, `Hash::of`). A **stateful** object — a response, a session, a config overlay — may use `set…`
and `add…`, which is not a mutation of a value and so not a question for
[`core-api/nothing-mutates`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#nothing-mutates "No Core member mutates its argument and none takes a reference").

`…OrNull`, `…Safe` and `…Ex` are banned, and so is `try…` on every verb but one. The exception is
`tryParse` ([`expressions/try-parse`](/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#try-parse "A failable single-string parse is spelled tryParse, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it")), for a class whose `parse` takes exactly one `string` and can
fail: a malformed string is a *failure*, not the absence `?T` means, and `as ?T` never targets a class, so
without it `Core\Uri` and `Core\Uuid` would have no non-throwing spelling at all. The `…Safe` half of the
ban reads the suffix as a claim about failure; a suffix that is an ordinary adjective of the subject is
untouched, which is how `Core\Db\Schema::applySafe` is admitted — it is named for the grade of the steps it
will run and is the more refusing of the two, not the quiet one.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#failure-throws" title="A Core member throws on failure and returns ?T for absence; false is never an answer"><code>core-api/failure-throws</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#symmetric-names" title="A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste"><code>core-api/symmetric-names</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#try-parse" title="A failable single-string parse is spelled tryParse, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it"><code>expressions/try-parse</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0145.md">record 0145</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="symmetric-names">

## A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#symmetric-names"><code>core-api/symmetric-names</code></a>
</div>

A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name: `encode`/`decode`, `split`/`join`, `pack`/`unpack`,
`escape`/`unescape`, `trimStart`/`trimEnd`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`, `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`,
`first`/`last`. If one half exists, the other half's spelling is decided by rule rather than chosen.

Which *pair* to reach for is also a rule: `encode`/`decode` when the other side is a machine format —
JSON, serialization, base64 — and `parse`/`format` when a human writes or reads it, as with time, CSV and
URIs. That removes the per-member judgement call PHP made differently every time, and it means a reader who
has found one half knows the other's name without looking.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#verb-lexicon" title="A member's verb predicts its return type, and …OrNull, …Safe, …Ex and every try… but tryParse are banned"><code>core-api/verb-lexicon</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#members-are-full-words" title="A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list"><code>core-api/members-are-full-words</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="one-name-one-signature">

## One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#one-name-one-signature"><code>core-api/one-name-one-signature</code></a>
</div>

One name has one signature. There is no overloading, and optional arguments are the only variance a
member's parameter list may have. Two behaviours therefore need two names, and which two is decided by the
verb lexicon ([`core-api/verb-lexicon`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#verb-lexicon "A member's verb predicts its return type, and …OrNull, …Safe, …Ex and every try… but tryParse are banned")) and the symmetric-name rule
([`core-api/symmetric-names`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#symmetric-names "A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste")) rather than by whoever writes the second one.

This is the rule that keeps a family from regrowing. PHP has eleven sort functions and twelve `strpos`
variants because each new behaviour could be a new name in the same shape; here it has to be a name that
predicts its own return type, or an enum-typed option on the member that already exists
([`core-api/no-mode-strings`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#no-mode-strings "A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt")). Where two members genuinely take different things and answer different
things, that is not a second spelling ([`core-api/each-door-takes-a-different-thing`](/docs/rules/core-api/lifetimes-and-absences/#each-door-takes-a-different-thing "Two members are not a second spelling when each takes a different thing and answers a different thing")).

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#verb-lexicon" title="A member's verb predicts its return type, and …OrNull, …Safe, …Ex and every try… but tryParse are banned"><code>core-api/verb-lexicon</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/lifetimes-and-absences/#two-cache-tiers" title="Cross-request state is reached through a member per tier, each with its own contract, never one API with a flag"><code>core-api/two-cache-tiers</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/statements/names-and-require/#nothing-gets-a-second-name" title="A declaration is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with"><code>statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0051.md">record 0051</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="members-are-full-words">

## A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#members-are-full-words"><code>core-api/members-are-full-words</code></a>
</div>

A member name is a full word. Class names may abbreviate, but only from a closed list — `Str`, `Arr`, `Fs`,
`Io`, `Uri`, `Db`, `Id` — and members may not, except the conventional mathematical spellings `abs`, `min`,
`max` and `sqrt`. So `Core\Str::length`, never `Core\Str::len`.

Abbreviation is where a naming convention stops being mechanical: PHP resolved it separately for every
function and produced `strlen` beside `str_word_count`. A closed list at the class level and no discretion
at the member level removes the judgement call entirely, at the cost of a few extra characters at every
call site.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>strlen</code> is <code>Core\Str::length</code>, not <code>Core\Str::len</code></p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#identifier-casing" title="An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error"><code>core-api/identifier-casing</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun" title="A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it"><code>core-api/a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0011.md">record 0011</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="identifier-casing">

## An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#identifier-casing"><code>core-api/identifier-casing</code></a>
</div>

Every user-written identifier is checked against exactly one pattern for its category, and a mismatch is a
hard compile error — not a lint, not a warning.

| Category | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Class, interface, enum | `PascalCase` | `HTTPClient`, `Comparable` |
| `type` alias, at file scope or in a body | `PascalCase` | `UserId` |
| Enum case | `PascalCase` | `Active` |
| Namespace segment | `PascalCase` | `Core\Html\Markup` |
| Method, instance or `static` | `camelCase` | `parseXMLPayload` |
| Property, any visibility | `camelCase` | `userName` |
| Parameter, local variable | `camelCase` | `$rowCount` |
| Class constant | `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` | `MAX_RETRIES` |

Built-in type keywords and language keywords are reserved words the grammar already lowercases and are not
checked. No identifier may begin with `_`, in any category, which is what leaves the rule exception-free:
with the constructor spelled as a word rather than with underscores, there is no reserved name a casing
rule has to be told to skip.

The check needs no name resolution — every category is already its own syntax node — so it runs before
anything is resolved and its diagnostic carries a mechanically derived rename. It is decided while the
standard library is unwritten because renaming a member later is a breaking change with no deprecation path
([`statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name`](/docs/rules/statements/names-and-require/#nothing-gets-a-second-name "A declaration is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with")). The cost is a structural break from PHP: `snake_case`
source does not compile, and a converted name that collides with another after rewriting is the one case a
converter cannot settle alone.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>PHP checks legal characters and never case, so <code>snake_case</code> identifiers do not compile here</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="casing-checks-the-leading-character">

## Only the leading character's case is checked, so `HTTPClient` and `HttpClient` both pass

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#casing-checks-the-leading-character"><code>core-api/casing-checks-the-leading-character</code></a>
</div>

Only the first character's case is checked. The rest of an identifier need only be alphanumeric ASCII, so a
run of consecutive capitals is accepted anywhere after the first: `HTTPClient`, `IOStream`,
`parseXMLPayload` and `HTTPXMLParser` all pass, and so do `HttpClient`, `IoStream` and `parseXmlPayload`.

An earlier rule required acronyms written as one word. It was revoked because deciding whether `HTTP` *is*
an acronym needs a maintained dictionary the compiler would have to ship and keep current, and even with
one it has no answer for two adjacent acronyms. Checking a single character needs neither a dictionary nor
a judgement, which is what makes the diagnostic's suggested rename always correct.

The cost is that a codebase can still be internally inconsistent about acronyms. That is accepted: the rule
exists to make a name's *category* legible from its spelling, and the leading character carries all of it.

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#identifier-casing" title="An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error"><code>core-api/identifier-casing</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#casing-has-no-suppression" title="There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category"><code>core-api/casing-has-no-suppression</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0029.md">record 0029</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-syntax/src/casing.rs"><code>crates/nvs-syntax/src/casing.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/a-class-name-must-be-pascalcase.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/a-class-name-must-be-pascalcase.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="casing-has-no-suppression">

## There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#casing-has-no-suppression"><code>core-api/casing-has-no-suppression</code></a>
</div>

There is no configuration, no per-project override and no suppression annotation for a casing error. A name
that must violate the convention — because it mirrors an external wire format, or because a converter
produced it unmodified — does not compile until it is renamed, and a mapping layer is the only route.

A suppression attribute would be the first compiler-level opt-out of any kind in this language, which is a
larger precedent than the rule it would soften; and a warning tier would be ignored indefinitely, since
every other diagnostic here is an error. The same reasoning covers the other spelling rules: a rule whose
whole value is that the author decided is worth nothing if the author can skip it.

The stance is the piece most likely to be revisited, and only under pressure from a concrete boundary that
does not exist yet. The question would then be whether *that one* boundary needs an escape, not whether the
check should have been a warning.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Unlike Rust's <code>#[allow(non_snake_case)]</code> there is no attribute, pragma or per-file opt-out; a name mirroring an external format is renamed or does not compile</p>
</aside>

</div>
